svg.text: My brokerage routine as one record: the Watchlist
a single aggregate, decided by me · two things outside that I can't control: the market and the broker · 16 scenarios, 5 of them real
yellow: people · pale: the record, with its five parts · green: a view · pink: outside · scenario cards carry the tag of the part that answers them
THE ONE RECORD · A SINGLE AGGREGATE
decided by me · every company I own or consider, and everything I do about them
report read, as of its date
completed, in full or in part
rules: a company is listed once · an order completes or expires only if it was requested
a closed review never changes · the broker's numbers win over mine
everything else is a suggestion: it goes through, and is marked
Scenarios: what can happen, and the part of the record that answers it
11 could happen: to check against my real routine
an IPO: the order comes first,
a new ticker or a new owner:
the stage becomes sold; it stays
on the list, or I stop following
the next review covers the gap
bad news about a company I own:
reviewed as in doubt; hold or sell
a source is down on review day:
the paycheck is still on its way:
the budget waits; so do orders
noted; it joins the next budget
seen at the broker; budget drops
a dip alert, cash to spare:
recorded in part; the rest expires
the order copies the price I
saw; the limit does the guarding
a double tap on the phone:
the second is marked a duplicate
1 I add a company to the watchlist, with the reason. An IPO can go straight to an order instead.
2 Every two weeks Claude Code reads the list, gathers prices, P/E and news from the market, and reads my numbers from the broker.
3 Claude Code builds the report, with the date and source of every number.
4 I read the report. Any difference from the broker is explained before anything else.
5 I review each company and decide: buy, sell or hold. The paycheck is the budget.
6 I request orders at the broker, each with a limit price, and record them on the watchlist.
7 The broker answers: completed, in full or in part, or expired. I record what I saw.
8 Splits, dividends and alerts arrive from the broker on their own. Each becomes a fact on the watchlist.
Suggestions, not rules: nothing here is refused
• Watch a company before buying it.
• Stay within the paycheck plus spare cash.
• Each exception goes through and is marked, so the next
Outside, and not in my control
• The market: prices, news, and what companies do.
• The broker: my money and shares, and whether an order completes.
Three models of the same routine
picked out of one long history
seeing the routine as one story
